item.description: A hands-on setup guide for Claude Code covering 32 tested skills and 8 MCP servers, with install commands meant to be copied verbatim. It draws the line between the two extension types: skills are packaged prompts and workflows that make the model better at a given task, while MCP servers are local processes that let it touch files, browsers and external APIs. Most of them trigger automatically, and the author notes the npm examples may be missing a repo prefix.

item.title: [infoq] 四分之一PR是“AI垃圾”！Linux基金会发布新报告：AI写代码快了52%，开源维护者却更累了
item.description: A Linux Foundation report released Oct 20, “Navigating Open Source Software Development in the Generative AI Era,” sponsored by Red Hat, finds generative AI cut coding time by 52% on average. But maintainers estimate roughly 25% of incoming PRs are low-quality “AI slop,” rising to 31% on large projects, while 59% report more contributions overall. 21% of respondents say complex tasks actually take longer with AI.

item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] Railse：一个人同时开几个 AI 编程 agent，审批推到手机上点一下
item.description: Railse routes approval prompts from Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI through one local daemon and a single rule set: read-only and in-project edits pass automatically, network and irreversible commands always ask, and anything the rules can't classify is pushed to your phone via Web Push. Approvals can be saved as rules, except outbound and irreversible ones. If the daemon is unreachable for 30 seconds, the CLIs fall back to their own prompts. v0.1.2, Apache 2.0.

item.title: [v2ex] [硬件] RAID 换盘为什么要一块一块来：连换三块盘把阵列弄异常了，顺便说说重建期间要盯什么
item.description: A customer's array went abnormal after three drives were swapped back to back, prompting a write-up of the basics: RAID 5 tolerates one offline drive and RAID 6 two, and a replacement doesn't count as healthy until its rebuild finishes and status returns to Optimal — pulling the next drive before that exceeds fault tolerance. The post also covers what to watch during rebuild and common mistakes like incompatible drive models and slot mix-ups.

item.title: [v2ex] [Apple] M6 vs M4 Pro, M6 确实有意思
item.description: A Mac mini with M6 (12+12 cores, 32GB) was compared against one with M4 Pro (14+20 cores, 64GB): Geekbench single-core 4000 vs 3400, multi-core 22000 vs 25800, Metal 90000 vs 115000, with everyday use feeling identical. The real gap shows in Lightroom 15.6 noise reduction running on the NPU, where 20 45MP RAWs took 2m28s on M6 versus 5m12s on M4 Pro. The author concludes M6 makes the base M4 Pro hard to justify.

item.description: A self-described Claude account reseller names two decisive ban factors. First, the payment environment: since October 18 virtual cards can no longer open Max plans, and only local physical cards tied to a single account, with the issuing bank matching the login IP, avoid a KYC prompt. Second, usage — running distillation-style workloads gets accounts banned anyway. He calls ban-replacement guarantees a gimmick and recommends a clean residential IP.

It also covers JDK 28 Early Access Build 19 and GlassFish 8.0.5. Useful for teams planning around the JDK 28 upgrade.

item.title: [infoq] Cloudflare 的 OHTTP 网关拒绝解密通过 Cloudflare 传入的请求
item.description: Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of its OHTTP Gateway, a hosted endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP (RFC 9458) requests on behalf of origin servers. The notable constraint: it refuses to decrypt traffic arriving through Cloudflare Workers or proxied hosts, since the relay hop that sees client IPs and the decrypting hop must be run by unrelated operators. Cloudflare ships no relay server; its older Privacy Gateway is now called OHTTP Relay.

item.description: QCon Shanghai 2026, hosted by InfoQ China from October 22 to 24, drew more than 1,200 attendees and 140 speakers from 70 companies, with the program centered on how AI moves from agent engineering into production delivery. In the opening keynote, Geekbang editor-in-chief Zhao Yuying argued that more agents isn't automatically better, since communication cost and error propagation grow, and that teams should focus on whether tasks finish and results can be verified.

item.title: [infoq] 模型好选，搜索难做：一个投研Agent的两年开发历程
item.description: Chen Wan writes a paid research brief on the energy-storage and lithium supply chain for roughly 4,000 subscribers. He recently deleted two files he had maintained for years: cleaner.py, which scraped web pages, and sites.yaml, a list of 387 vetted sources, replacing them with a search API that plugs directly into his agent. Tencent Cloud's Yuanbao search returned page summaries, question-relevant passages and per-result publish times rather than one-line abstracts.

item.description: DeepTutor is an open-source GitHub project from HKUDS positioned as "Lifelong Personalized Tutoring," with documentation hosted at deeptutor.info and a separate page for collaborating with the team. item.title: [infoq] 中层技术经理要么重新学技术，要么考虑退休：前 Stripe 工程高管警告，未来三年工程管理将彻底变样
item.description: Will Larson, who managed engineering at Stripe and Uber and later served as CTO at Carta and Calm, argues on The Pragmatic Engineer podcast that the traditional engineering-management role may disappear within three years, leaving mid-level managers to either get hands-on again or consider retiring. He made that move himself, going from a roughly 250-person org at Carta to a 25-person team at Imprint, and expects tech-lead-managers to be in demand.

item.title: [infoq] Android Bench 2 新增对长周期任务、智能评估和连续评分的支持
item.description: Google released Android Bench 2.0, adding long-horizon tasks (LHT) such as dependency upgrades, new features, building apps from scratch and porting cross-platform apps, work that takes engineers days to a week. Scoring moved from binary pass/fail to a continuous completion rate weighing functionality, visual fidelity and regressions, plus agent-based evaluation. Claude Opus 5.5 currently leads with a 32% LHT pass rate, ahead of GPT 6 Astra at 28%.

item.title: [hackernews] We should be more ambitious with the software we build
item.description: An essay arguing that developers should be more ambitious about what they build, using pgrust — Michael Malis's Rust rewrite of Postgres — as the case in point. The author acknowledges the widespread skepticism toward AI-generated projects, then notes that pgrust's testing is thorough enough to have surfaced real Postgres bugs, including SP-GiST numeric errors, a JSONPath format cache bug, pgcrypto failures and a money overflow. Relevant to anyone judging where AI-assisted work actually holds up

item.title: [github_trending] pbakaus/impeccable
item.description: Impeccable is a design guidance package for AI coding agents: one skill, 24 commands, live browser iteration and 62 deterministic detector rules, installed with npx impeccable install and initialized via /impeccable init. It builds on Anthropic's frontend-design skill and records product truth in PRODUCT.md to suppress the usual tells, such as Inter everywhere, purple-to-blue gradients and cards nested in cards. Useful for developers whose AI-written frontends all look alike.

item.title: [github_trending] makecindy/cindy
item.description: Cindy is an Apache-2.0 open-source AI agent from makecindy that is meant to work out of the box. It links your work computer, home desktop, laptop and phone, uses the models and subscriptions you already pay for, and does real work on your own machines. It's aimed at developers who want a customizable, self-hosted agent without building the scaffolding themselves.

Each skill is a self-contained folder you install individually; the first, landing-page-design, covers intake questions, page structure, conversion copy and a visual system of type, spacing, radius and motion. Useful if you want AI-generated pages to follow a consistent design standard.

item.title: [hackernews] Sebastian Raschka's from-scratch video course on building reasoning models
item.description: Sebastian Raschka has released a from-scratch video course on building reasoning models: more than 11 hours of coding footage covering evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning and distillation, written in Python and PyTorch. It's aimed at developers who want to see how reasoning models are actually trained and evaluated, rather than just calling an API.

item.title: [github_trending] JetBrains/thinkrail

JetBrains says full extension support comes next, so the IDE can generate the tools it needs from how you actually work. It targets developers who want agents handling whole tasks rather than autocomplete.

item.description: Two US senators say the Trump administration is breaking the law by withholding a FISA court decision while pressing Congress to renew what the report calls America's most sweeping surveillance program. The clash matters because lawmakers are being asked to reauthorize the program without being able to see how the court has ruled on spying on Americans.

It treats an agent's runtime as a tunable operating system, which makes it relevant to developers who already lean on coding agents daily and want more stable, controllable behavior.

item.title: [juejin] 一键还原任意网站，这套 Playwright + 多 Agent 工程流太猛了
item.description: Developer alien walks through ai-website-cloner-template, a GitHub template you clone locally and drive from Claude Code via a /clone-website skill to rebuild any site as code. It uses Playwright to screenshot three viewports, walks the DOM with getComputedStyle to harvest design tokens, and simulates scroll, click and hover states. Tested against juejin.cn, the author measured roughly 70% UI fidelity, with mobile layouts holding up better.
